messages.subject: [GGIR 1.5-10] Part 5 error : Error in aggregate.data.frame
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

First of all, thanks for this tool box which is very useful for our project.

I have some problems since I am using the latest version of the GGIR (1.5-10 with R 3.4). I didn't have any problem when i was using the older version of GGIR 1.2-2 (which was installed automatically when i was using R 3.1). As I was interested by the part 5 report I installed the R 3.4 and a newest version of the GGIR. Since, but only for one of my participant (out of 10) I have the following error message :

''Report part 5
 loading all the milestone data from part 5 this can take a few minutes
 generating output for every parameter configurations...
 WW-30-100-400-T5A5
Error in aggregate.data.frame(A, by = list(A$filename), FUN = df) :
  no rows to aggregate''

Anyone has already had this kind of error ?

Best regards

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Very High ENMO Outputs When Recalibration Fails
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Very High ENMO Outputs When Recalibration Fails
messages.body_plain:
Sorry to hear that Taren. It may be valuable then to advise to all:
- Pilot process your data while you are stilling running your study, this to identify poorly performing accelerometers early on. Do not wait till all data has been collected, because then it is too late.
- Report issues with accelerometers to the manufacturer. Depending on your warranty conditions they may have a solution for you.

Further, it may be informative if people could reply to this message with reports of how this issue affected their study such that we can get some idea of whether it is
specific to an accelerometer brand, population, or period in time.

I know from Séverine's data that it was GENEActiv, collected in 2012/2013, age range 60-83, and affected a really small fraction of the files (< 0.1%). My understanding is that GENEActiv has undergone some upgrades since then, so this may not apply to future studies.

Vincent

> > > we also had issues with some of our devices. If you look at the device numbers corresponding to the files with issues, do you find the same devices?
> > > In our experience few devices started to have some weird results after some time (sometimes due to water inside the device), calibration method could not always correct for these issues and we had to exclude these devices and the recorded data from our analyses.

> > > >
> > > > For files where the recalibration completes, the data looks good - the MVPA estimates are what I would expect. However, for files where the output in part 2 reads "recalibration not done because not enough points on all sides of the sphere", I get very high ENMO values (>400) and consequently very high MVPA output (>16 hours).
> > > >
> > > > When I inspect the data plots I can see that the accelerometer values are too high (image attached). As you can see in the plot, there is a period of time before the device was actually worn, and i'm wondering if it's trying to calibrate using this data?
> > > >
> > > > I've tried:
> > > > Running the script with do.imp = FALSE
> > > > With varying types of "strategy ="
> > > >
> > > > I'm wondering if this is a problem with our protocol (i.e., with non-wear time at the beginning of the measurement period), a problem with the device (i.e., sensor problems), or something I can fix in GGIR?
> > > >
> > > > Appreciate and suggestions.
> > > >
> > > > Thanks,
> > > > Taren

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.5-12
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

A new version of GGIR is now online.

See the NEWS log <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html> for a detailed overview of the changes.

Main updates:
- Jairo Migueles, a PhD-student from the University of Granada in Spain has joint the developers team. He has been making valuable contributions already. Welcome Jairo!
- We improved the code quality of GGIR by making the code more readable and better covered by tests that help guarantee consistent functionality in the future.
- We discovered that function g.part5 had the timezone of the United Kingdom hard-coded into it, this is now fixed.
-Functions g.part3, g.part4 and g.part5 are now independent of metric ENMO to work, argument acc.metric allows the user to select which metric to use to describe behavior. We have not added this functionality to g.shell.GGIR yet, but will do in the next release.
- It is now possible to work with the MAD acceleration metric as used in some papers in recent years. Although, the ENMO metric is still my personal favorite, we agreed that it is good to facilitate comparisons between metrics and let you as user decide.

Finally, congratulations to all the people who managed to get their work published <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/wiki/Publication-list>: The year 2017 is starting to look like a very successful year for GGIR. Please keep remembering to acknowledge the use of GGIR and version number in your papers, see also section 7 in the vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#citing-ggir>.

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.subject: Can you extract data for time windows defined down to the minute rather than the hour?
messages.subject_clean: Can you extract data for time windows defined down to the minute rather than the hour?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent

Thanks so much for creating GGIR and for making it available open source.

I have recently started working with physical activity data recorded using GENEActiv accelerometers. One of my tasks is to extract variables relating to specific time points within the data collection period and I’m hoping to be able to use GGIR to do this. However, reading the documentation, it looks as though the coding only allows data extraction on the hour – is it possible to alter the granularity here so that I can select time windows at the minute level?

Best wishes

Sarah Price

messages.subject: Re: Can you extract data for time windows defined down to the minute rather than the hour?
messages.subject_clean: Can you extract data for time windows defined down to the minute rather than the hour?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarah,

I think you can do this with the time windows, e.g. to get 8:30 am - 3:15 pm the window would be (8.5,15.25). Another option is to generate the timestamped csv epoch files using epochvalues2csv in g.part2.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Timezone and start_time
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent,

Thank you for developing this very useful R package! I am using it (ver 1.5-12) to extract variables from geneactiv data but I am having this problem.

I ran part 1 and 2 of the package and I set the timezone as Europe/Amsterdam (desirestz="Europe/Amsterdam"). However, looking at the part 2 summary and meta data it seems that the start_time and the first timestamp are not correct. The start_time (and the first timestamp) is always 18:15, but the data collection started at 19:00 in Europe/Amsterdam timezone.

I ran again part 1 and 2 on a couple of files without changing the timezone but I obtained the same start_time (18:15).

I hope you could help me with it.

Kind regards,

Sonia
